posterior meniscotibial ligament (medial: Ligament attaching the posterior horn of the medial meniscus to the tibia; it lies next to the part of the meniscus that tears most often.
posterior obturator tubercle: Small prominence on the posterior margin of the obturator foramen; the obturator membrane attaches to it.
posterior process of talus: Posterior process; the FHL tendon passes in the groove between its two tubercles.
posterior sacral foramina: Posterior sacral foramina; the posterior rami of the sacral nerves emerge through them.
posterior sacro-iliac ligament: Strong ligament of short and long fibres behind the sacroiliac joint.
posterior sternoclavicular ligament: Posterior capsular thickening of the joint; in posterior dislocation the great vessels behind it are at risk.
posterior superior iliac spine: Posterior end of the iliac crest; the dimple in the skin over it (dimple of Venus) marks the S2 level.
posterior surface of arytenoid cartilage: Posterior surface; covered by the transverse and oblique arytenoid muscles.
posterior surface of fibula: Posterior surface of the fibula; soleus and FHL arise from it.
posterior surface of humerus: Posterior surface of the humerus; it carries the triceps heads and the radial groove.
posterior surface of petrous part: Surface facing the posterior cranial fossa; the internal acoustic meatus opens on it.
posterior surface of radius: Posterior surface of the radius; APL and EPB arise from it.
posterior surface of scapula: Posterior surface divided in two by the spine of the scapula.
posterior surface of tibia: Posterior surface of the tibia; it carries the soleal line.
posterior surface of ulna: Posterior surface of the ulna; the deep extensors arise from it.
posterior talocalcaneal ligament: Short ligament closing the subtalar joint behind.
posterior talofibular ligament: Strong ligament from the lateral malleolus to the posterior process of the talus; rarely torn.
posterior tibiofibular ligament: Strong ligament holding the distal tibiofibular syndesmosis from behind.
posterior tibiotalar ligament: The strongest, deep part of the deltoid ligament.
posterior tubercle of atlas: Prominence in the middle of the posterior arch; rectus capitis posterior minor and the nuchal ligament attach to it.
posterior tubercle of transverse process: Posterior prominence of a cervical transverse process; the scalene muscles attach to it.
posteromedial surface of fibula: Posteromedial surface of the fibula; tibialis posterior arises from it.
procerus muscle: At the root of the nose it pulls down the medial ends of the eyebrows, making horizontal wrinkles at the bridge of the nose.
promontory: Anterosuperior edge of the sacrum; the posterior boundary of the pelvic inlet and a reference point in obstetric measurement.
pronator quadratus: Deep muscle joining the radius and ulna in the distal quarter of the forearm; the main muscle of pronation. Anterior interosseous nerve.
pronator teres: Two-headed forearm muscle; it inserts into the middle of the radial shaft and pronates. Median nerve.
pronator tuberosity: Rough area on the lateral surface of the radius; pronator teres inserts here.
proximal phalanx of fifth finger of foot: Proximal bone of the little toe; the phalanges of the foot are shorter than those of the hand.
proximal phalanx of fifth finger of hand: Proximal bone of the little finger; its base articulates with the metacarpal head and its head with the middle or distal phalanx.
proximal phalanx of first finger of foot: Proximal bone of the big toe; the phalanges of the foot are shorter than those of the hand.
proximal phalanx of first finger of hand: Proximal bone of the thumb; its base articulates with the metacarpal head and its head with the middle or distal phalanx.
proximal phalanx of fourth finger of foo: Proximal bone of the 4th toe; the phalanges of the foot are shorter than those of the hand.
proximal phalanx of fourth finger of han: Proximal bone of the ring finger; its base articulates with the metacarpal head and its head with the middle or distal phalanx.
proximal phalanx of second finger of foo: Proximal bone of the 2nd toe; the phalanges of the foot are shorter than those of the hand.
proximal phalanx of second finger of han: Proximal bone of the index finger; its base articulates with the metacarpal head and its head with the middle or distal phalanx.
proximal phalanx of third finger of foot: Proximal bone of the 3rd toe; the phalanges of the foot are shorter than those of the hand.
proximal phalanx of third finger of hand: Proximal bone of the middle finger; its base articulates with the metacarpal head and its head with the middle or distal phalanx.
psoas major: Long muscle from the T12–L5 vertebrae to the lesser trochanter; the most powerful flexor of the thigh. The lumbar plexus forms within the muscle. Branches of the lumbar plexus.
pterygoid canal: Canal at the root of the pterygoid process; the nerve of the pterygoid canal (Vidian nerve) passes through it.
pterygoid fossa: Fossa between the two pterygoid plates; medial pterygoid arises here.
pterygoid hamulus: Hook at the tip of the medial plate; the tensor veli palatini tendon turns around it.
pterygoid notch: Notch at the lower end of the two plates; a process of the palatine bone fits into it.
pterygoid process: Process extending downwards from the sphenoid; it consists of two plates.
pterygospinous ligament: Ligament between the lateral pterygoid plate and the spine of the sphenoid; if it ossifies it can compress branches of the mandibular nerve.
pterygospinous process: Process on the posterior border of the lateral plate; a ligament joins it to the spine of the sphenoid.
pubic crest: Upper border of the body of the pubis; rectus abdominis and pyramidalis attach to it.
pubic symphysis: Fibrocartilaginous joint uniting the two pubic bones in front; it loosens in pregnancy under the influence of relaxin.
pubic tubercle: Prominence at the lateral end of the pubic crest; the inguinal ligament attaches to it, and it is a landmark in hernia examination.
pubis: Anteroinferior part of the hip bone.
pubo-analis muscle: Fibres of levator ani forming a U-shaped sling behind the rectum that creates the anorectal angle; essential for continence.
pubococcygeus muscle: Main part of levator ani, running from the pubis to the coccyx; it supports the pelvic organs and can be damaged in childbirth.
pubofemoral ligament: Ligament from the superior pubic ramus to the capsule; limits excessive abduction.
pyramidalis muscle: Small triangular muscle at the very bottom of the rectus sheath, from the pubis to the linea alba; tenses the linea alba. Absent in some people.
quadrangular membrane: Fibroelastic membrane between the epiglottis and the arytenoid cartilage; its free lower edge forms the false vocal fold (vestibular ligament).
quadrate ligament: Binds the neck of the radius to the lower border of the radial notch of the ulna; limits supination.
quadrate tubercle: Prominence on the intertrochanteric crest; quadratus femoris inserts here.
quadratus femoris muscle: Powerful lateral rotator running from the ischial tuberosity to the intertrochanteric crest.
quadratus lumborum muscle: Posterior abdominal wall muscle between the iliac crest, the 12th rib and the transverse processes of the lumbar vertebrae. Nerves: T12–L4. It bends the trunk sideways and fixes the 12th rib during inspiration.
quadratus plantae muscle: Attaches from the calcaneus to the flexor digitorum longus tendon and corrects its line of pull.
